8747412007271928012:
Dunhuang Song Lyrics refer to hundreds of folk songs and lyrics works from the Tang and Five Dynasties discovered in the Mogao Grottoes at Mingsha Mountain in Dunhuang, Gansu, including "Collection of Cloud Ballads".  
In terms of genre, their discovery fills the gap in the evolution of ci before it was finalized in Book of Flowers. Prior to this, most people believed that ci formed in the Five Dynasties and were unaware that songs and ci were already widely used in the Tang Dynasty. 
In terms of content, Dunhuang Song Lyrics have rich themes and simple language, vividly recording the life scenes of Dunhuang and the Hexi region from the Tang and Five Dynasties to the early Song Dynasty, especially presenting a precious picture of multi-ethnic integration. At the same time, the content of these songs and lyrics corrects the misunderstanding that early lyrics only included literati works such as Book of Flowers, mostly singing of love between men and women, and taking gracefulness as the orthodox style.

8746481561035527419:
Those who walk at night might sometimes encounter a line of Little girls dressed in red, silently marching forward. The one at the front looks the most pitiful, often reaching out to Passerby and pleading, "Hold my hand for a while, I'm afraid of the dark." 
One night, a late-returning peddler took pity on the red-clad Girl at the front and took her hand. The moment he did, he realized her grip was like an icy iron shackle—impossible to shake off! Terrified, he tried to run, but his legs wouldn’t obey. Helpless, he was forced to follow the procession of red-clad girls. 
They moved faster and faster, deliberately steering into desolate woods. The peddler tried to scream, but his throat felt blocked. In horror, he noticed his own hand turning Qing and cold. Looking at the girls again, their eyes were hollow—nothing like a Kid’s. Eventually, he found himself dazedly joining the end of the line, his bones feeling shattered, his body now clad in red like the others, his gaze growing vacant. 
Elders say those are replacement souls "led" into the procession. The leader’s hand is a soul-snaring chain—once taken, you must fill her place, doomed to walk forever.
